I strongly recommend this game to anyone even remotely considering it. It has two very strong game modes. One is similar to games like Vampire Survivors and Soulstone Survivors (among others in the genre) and is a reverse bullet hell game where you build synergies between your spells and disks to get crazy combos going off. The other game mode is more akin to something like a mix between Tiny Rogues and Wizard of Legend. It's hard to explain, but I've been having a blast in both of these game modes and they feel different enough to give entirely different experiences while building off very solid core mechanics that bring something new to the genre. There are a couple of minor issues, though the developer appears to be very active and focused on addressing problems as they arise with a rapidity that would put larger studios to shame. All together, I would give this game a very solid buy recommendation.

很有意思的肉鸽游戏，包含一个闯关模式和一个幸存者模式，值回票价。游戏的逻辑很简单，满足条件后，法术和圆盘连锁激活（不像其他游戏需要你记住超武的搭配），圆盘、法术、道具种类十分丰富，能凑出千奇百怪的搭配，build凑的好就是全自动释放、“莫名其妙”地清了满屏的怪，爽感倍增。很适合时不时拿起来玩一局，推荐。

键鼠操作有点难受。 几个格子放的东西信息不清晰，战斗时候都不能迅速的知道自己的技能为啥不触发，下次什么时候可以触发 第一局死亡就直接游戏卡住了。啥也不能操作只能强关游戏 玩了一会的再次编辑 说实话挺失望了，发售之前以为可以跟传说法师媲美。 打通关一次之后居然就自动进了个生存模式的房间，也就是吸血鬼幸存者模式。 并且第一次出现新手教程居然是打完一次普通模式，再打一次生存模式后出现的 ？？无法理解这个设计思路 2个模式的局外加成完全独立。生存模式的局外加成更为丰富，普通模式的加成就几条简单的线路搞个树形图，仿佛粗制滥造。 可是这游戏的商店页放出来的图都是普通模式的，像极了手游广告，看到个感兴趣的题材，点进去玩了2分钟发现广告内容仅是开头。 普通模式其实玩起来还挺不错的，可以构建出有意思的bd。 生存模式就开局随几个卡，选了之后大概率都是这几个卡的升级，很难出新卡，基本就是开局有啥后面就是啥，而且没有普通模式下的搭配快感，就是全自动的放啊放。 最后一句话 普通模式还能玩玩。幸存者模式。垃圾！垃圾！垃圾！

全面拉踩 首先这个价格方面，其实本来58是能接受的，但前面有一个20的原点计划，就显得58有点贵了； 这游戏和原点计划在幸存者模式的内容上抬举点说不相上下，但多出来的爬塔模式并不出彩，我愿称之为幸存者模式武器解锁器，因为太无聊了，一路砍砍砍连个随机事件都没有，毫无策略性，甚至如果他不是从地下室往上爬，看山去和爬塔很像，并且也找不到更好的词来形容这个模式，我都不会称呼这是爬塔模式……幸存者模式也是打怪爬塔模式也是打怪，那我为什么不直接玩幸存者模式呢，还省的一层层往上爬； 其次，圆盘的触发方式过于简单，以及圆盘释放一些法术必须一个个放而不能一股脑放出来，再加上过热的设计，导致上限远不如原点计划，也让我缺少了一些智力上的优越感，当然也大大降低了上手门槛，不过对于之前有过类似体验的玩家来说就不太吸引人了； 再次，三系元素有点少； 再再次，不知道为什么，这游戏给我感觉一卡一卡的，虽然帧数一直是60； 最后是最忍受不了的问题，鼠标玩家体验极差，原点计划已经够糟了，这游戏做的比他还垃圾，这种先适配手柄再强行把鼠标操作套到手柄操作上的行为，不像是2023年的游戏，而像是十年前的盗版移植游戏。 只能说，玩这个真不如玩原点计划，建议大伙去买原点计划，说不定他还能出创意工坊。

还可以，就是有几种怪设计的真的让人有点脑淤血，基本玩不起来纯近战，哪怕补点近战回血之类的也好，有几种远程怪和闪现到脸上的怪注定了走a会受不少伤害在这几种怪上。而到后面也基本都是法术圆盘套娃自动施法然后光走位了。还是希望多加点装备吧，并且希望每次抽物品是三选一，不然随机性有点太大。 然后就是幸存者模式下不知道为什么有些时候法术和圆盘特别难roll到，基本都是升级，都是到了固定等级再出的法术和圆盘，希望改成幸存者那样道具容易出一点

现阶段内容根本不值58，谁买谁傻，我是sb。 前面几个小时还有点意思，越到后面越无聊，生存模式无聊到犯困，爽感基本为0。 2023.10.24全成就后评价 游戏价格58，前面3小时左右的内容值50，后面的内容值8块，实际价格个人认为15左右可以接受，高于这个价格入纯纯搞自己心态。 1、随机性太高，很难玩到想玩的体系，玩物理随不出物理技能，玩电、火、雷法术不出该系列法术。 2、技能和道具完全失衡，光环类技能比如火环冰环和剑阵懂的都懂，公鸡套从未上过3件。 3、高低难度没什么卵区别，把天赋点满了也没增加多少游戏体验。 4、除了道具以外，没有任何东西能增加拾取范围，你想站着不动不操作是不可能的。 5、整个游戏的技能和状态没有“权重”这一玩意。 7、技能道具混合在一起3选1，不想要的技能无法剔除，想要的技能或者道具也没办法锁定。 总结：个人认为，想追求爽感的，建议去其他游戏，目前这个阶段，这个游戏没有体验感可言。 恶意猜想：这个游戏不设置技能和道具权重，是为了增加游戏寿命， 让你玩过前面几个小时无法退款。
很难受，法术尺子很大，随机性过高，开局抽了两个火系圆盘，结果包括重置以及购买新的法术，换了十几个法术都还是没见过火系的，就开局自带的一个，还魔法消耗巨高，我不知道是单纯的我脸黑还是什么？物理、火、冰、雷四属性随机能十几次一个都没有，全靠平砍往上刷，这游戏名是不是起错了？或者我就应该放弃天胡火属性的可能？我不理解，肉鸽有随机性是正常的，这随机的是不是过于离谱了？

一言以概之，noita+爬塔+vampire survivor，总之就是非常缝合。 操作上来说，攻击可以分为这些：武器的普通攻击，武器的蓄力攻击，武器魔法，圆盘魔法。 武器的攻击在幸存者模式是可选的，而在爬塔模式则是必有的，并且在前期也很重要，层数高了抓的build好可以逛该。 武器魔法是充能型的，每秒会自动回蓝，蓝够了才能放，可以切自动，但是爬塔模式自动放会降低回蓝速度，很坑；幸存者模式倒是建议开启。后期基本就是个圆盘触发器，毕竟放起来没什么负担[strike]也没什么伤害[/strike]，不像武器攻击会影响走位。 圆盘魔法则是满足圆盘触发条件时充能（百分比和固定值两种），蓝够了圆盘就会释放魔法，不过圆盘释放的方向和目标选定有点迷，我曾经给某个远离目标时每秒充能的圆盘挂上火球魔法，那个火球天天朝没人的地方打，搞不懂怎么想的，明明作为武器魔法的时候还是很安定的。 爬塔模式可能刚开始打不太过[strike]一层boss刷出蘑菇的话我大概率要当场饮恨[/strike]，多刷几盘把血点满可以有300血，然后还能每层楼回5血，再把药水效果+10点上，容错就相当充足了。
玩玩你做的B游戏吧，中个状态直接被中后期的小怪连到死。移动速度慢的跟来地牢逛街一样。主角是营养不良跑不动路还是天生残废？冲刺更是体感差到要命。

Before I start explaining why I do not reccommend this game, i'll tell you this : Yes, the game is fun. Yes, it has a survivor mode like the shovelware craze vampire survivor. Yes, you have a great deal of customization possible. Now, why I do NOT recommend this is... not simple. The game has "rules" that it does not follow. if something happens once, it will not be a fixed event. and by that I mean : You can not dash through enemies You can dash through one enemy Stun and paralyze can be applied to both the player and the enemies Stun and Paralyze do NOT need to be full to activate on the player, it is random from 1% to full and can happen at any time even without elemental attack done to the player. Stun and Paralyze NEED to be FULL to activate on the enemy, Disk needing status only need for the status to be FULL when it STATES needing it full, if it says "burning" or "cold status" then it needs full, if it says "Status damage" somehow it does not need to be full, this includes burning status... HALF THE TIME. the other half it wont work or work full time for no reasons. Disk needing an attack type means your WEAPON only. But sometime it will count disk bouncing around as a trigger as well even though that's not an attack. Disk linked with a melee effect (more on melee to follow) will be thrown automatically at an enemy to activate. for example if the spell says "Near the player" or "near the target" then the disk might be thrown upon activating so it can do the effect of the spell. But it never works if the disk needs a status, spell trigger (not damage) or attack. It will then activate on or near you at random. sometime prioritizing enemies. The melee is janky. Sure, it's a game about spells and stuff. I get that. Play for an hour and come back to apologize. You can not play this without using your weapon. you have a HUGE delay between attack combo and sometime mashing the attack button your character will just stand there doing nothing untill you hold the button instead. Ignore the tutorial, hitting attack button won't work when you need it to. and unfortunately holding it down, while it will activate your combo properly, will prevent you from moving for a full 1.5 seconds after release. And there are multiple relics... gear, item, whatever, that modify your weapon attack. Removing delay, repeating the last attack of the combo, better speed, more damage, more crit, more crit damage, change attack type, Slash and blunt counting as both at same time, etc. Damage is.... fine, I guess. Not too high, not too low. even on default difficulty this is fine. But there is no I-frame. you can bet your shorts you WILL be hit 50 time a second by an enemy swipe or aoe. Sometime it even shortens your dash or interrupts it. But the enemies do have I-frame. However... it's weird. you can strike 500 times a second with totem lightning, melee and some random multi-hit spell... but sometime if you only use the multi-hit spell it will ignore half of the damage or hits, or both. Go figure. Some enemies have a pattern. that's great... Good luck seeing it past stage 10. If you don't have the stamina shoe which doubles your dash stamina, you're not gonna have a good time. There is apparently an upgrade to stamina but I can't see it anywhere. Rules are ignored half the time. Samurai do a slash through the whole stage and it takes 1s to activate? great lemme dodge it when I see it again... nope it's now instant. nevermind it's 2 seconds. too late it's half a second. Did I say half a second? I meant back to 1 second. An enemy aoe needs to fill out to deal damage. nevermind it's instant even though it's empty. I mean half a fill, wait no! it's before it appear! You can dash through danger, says the tutorial. Except against bosses, two enemies slamming you against the wall, any projectile going towards you, any enemy melee attack... And when you somehow manage to mac and cheese your way to the end, you clear the normal mode! Hurray! Wanna play again? Here, have some forced survival mode just because we don't like our own game anymore. Speaking of the survival. It's just a basic square with grass and enemies coming at your from all sides. Except you don't have your weapon anymore. The upgrades says "clear the game with this weapon to unlock" and then it removes it from your hand and locks it forever. ain't that sweet... This is where "overheat" will actually be seen for the first time. Still no clue what it does, though. Nothing explains this in the game and it changes nothing, spells still fire at 50 times a second even when fully red. By the way, the "upgrade currency" is shared between both game mode, and by shared I mean you can spend it in either mode. Shared as in "Spending in survival removes it from normal mode too". And no, the upgrade are not shared, as far as I can tell. somehow I think it might have an effect somewhere... Anyway... I'm disappointed.

Spell Disk is a very fun game The whole point is to make your character a living firework thanks to disks that activate linked spells with conditions (it reminds path of exil on this point, except you get all the auto cast you can hope for) I love the system. The game is still a bit janky but very cool, there's a lot of thing to try, lot of spells, possible builds, artifacts ; multiple gamemode (roguelite, survivor and gamemodes post roguelite run) There's also starter stuff (hats&dresses) that can heavily affect the gameplay of each run Lot of diversity and magical explosions, very satisfying. It's a bit of a powertrip tho. The game isn't free either, mobs attack for real and get better stats as difficulty goes up (you will learn to fear the rain of feather... and the spores) But the fact is that your little sorceress becomes a walking cataclysm even for bosses (it's good and bad) I'd like the game to be a bit harder. And an option to go up faster in difficulties. But as I already played a lot, i'm not sure how revelant it is. You can also make your own challenges. I had fun playing with limitations, like no buying (felt more like a classic roguelite), no spells (surprisingly nice, but unsurprisingly hard), no more slots... It's not the best roguelite you ever played. But it's a unique and very fun one. And the 1.0 is coming soon when i'm writing this

游戏开发笔记02-Spell Disk（名字实在太朴实 幸存者类的割草爽游，通过搭配三大类装备（圆盘-触发条件；法术-触发内容；遗物-被动技能）来实现类似noita的编程式玩法 难度(4.5/10)，比较舒适的难度，玩起来不会很有压力 甚至给你塞了一个隔壁吸血鬼幸存者进去（完成度不高就是了 惯例上来先negative: *虽说作为一款爽游可以理解，但是后期特效堆满屏真的找不到boss位置 *怪物的设计不能说差，但是基本就是随机刷一地图怪让你漫无目的去打，我觉得作为一款动作性挺强的游戏来说，怪物的攻击形式，玩家和怪物的交互，可以更考究一些 *关卡重复性过强，有种本来15层可以结束，硬拉培养线给你来30层，游玩一轮时间翻倍的感觉 *培养解锁线过于简单，并没有让人推进的吸引力 *对于怪物身上每种元素累计满后触发的冰火雷效果，我仍然搞不太清楚..另外过热机制也缺乏解释 positive: *真的能做到每个操作流派（平A、蓄力攻击、蓄力按住不放、纯逛街躲子弹、翻滚强化...）都有非常独特的手感和玩法特性，打起来完完全全不一样的感觉，光这点我觉得足够我爽个十来小时，好评++ *刷初始要求不高，前中期应该是有刻意往你正在发展的流派塞对应的装备，好评；另外打最终boss的时候，好几把都是剩丝血莽过，我真的一度甚至怀疑他是不是做了放水机制...但是总的来说体验是相当正面的，护肝好评 *每次打通时候的配置会保存下来，让玩家可以拿去冲无尽、竞技场和BossRush，这样一套极品的构筑打完了一轮还有可玩的余地 could do better: *圆盘只影响到法术的释放频率，虽然前期来说这足够有趣，但从玩法多样性来说，是不是可以double释放次数之类的（我知道有遗物了 *圆盘和法术升级的词条过于随机，感觉不出强化的必要性，钱也不是很够花，开完槽买完东西就光了；个别法术就算强到很高，受限于触发条件和攻击范围，也会被隔壁0级全屏法术秒掉 *武器的平A、蓄力攻击前期稍显拖泥带水，但总体来说后期用来触发圆盘法术，手感是可以接受的，表现上可以优化一下

Horrible readability combined with a general misunderstanding of the concept of "challenge" to "let's spawn a million different things (including projectiles in certain cases) in the room" make this hard to recommend to most. Enemies vary from fodder on the lower levels to pinpoint, lightning-fast damage sponges on the higher ones. Charge attacks won't start if you dodge after you release the charge leading to a frustration when you manage to actually find the time to utilize the attack. I don't think I've ever said "What just hit me?" more than I have while playing this game. This is all especially unfortunate considering the titular spell disk mechanic holds some of the best synergy play I've seen in a roguelite in a while. Genuinely wish this was a better game

Spell Disk leaves a favorable first impression. But in the end, I don't recommend it due to several flaws that I can't overlook. The elephant in the room is the difficulty. If I beat the highest difficulty of a roguelite in <10 hours, dying during all the time only once and to an extra sequence (think of Heart in Slay the Spire), then the difficulty is just too low. With how slow most of the attacks on stages 1-2 are and how broken your build usually gets at stage 3, game never puts you into danger, save for that extra sequence. In fact, metaprogression made each run easier than the one before, despite the fact that I've always increased difficulty by a tiny bit the game allowed me to. Should I not have used metaprogression? I really don't like self-imposed challenges... The game also lacks identity. The dungeon crawling mode is kinda like Hades, but it also has a Survivor-like mode. I don't really care about the latter. I've had enough of mindless fireworks, and judging by the metaprogression tree—which is separate for each mode, by the way—it does not seem any different. But dungeon crawling mode is lacking, with very limited customization, and what is there isn't appealing to me. You can choose a starting weapon, but it stops being relevant very fast. It also has a wardrobe system, where you can choose starting items. These items usually provide both buff and debuff. I honestly looked at the wardrobe several times and always concluded with 'nah, default loadout seems best'. Why would I want to lock myself into a specific build before the game starts? Adaptability is important. Finally, the concept of combining spells in this game isn't even that interesting. It's all about acquisition of circles (mana generators, which trigger your spells) that will work for your build. Universal circles—ones that [i]just work[/i]—are the best ones, while very specific ones are a dud most of the time, and the difference is massive. If you get a bad couple of circles that won't reroll into something good, early game can be a slog. Spells themselves don't really matter much, what matters is how they fuel your circles. By maximizing your mana generation, spells trigger a lot, and therefore you deal high dps, and that's it. Noita this is not. It is a fun, but underbaked concept with lacking difficulty and identity crisis.

The core experience is somewhat similar to something like Noita or Path of Exile where you cast spells that activate other spells that activate other spells etc. etc. While reviews say that the game is relatively simple mechanically, I disagree. Often, your spell cast loops will depend on you either by attacking with your weapon light combo, heavy combo, dodging, or by casting your main spell. Your weapon combo's length and weapon damage depends on the given weapon, which can alter how your build develops over the course of a run. The game offers a surprising variety of spells, items, and "disks" (items that activate your spells when certain conditions are met, i.e. dealing a certain type of damage or walking a certain distance) that allow for a great amount of replayability. Meta-progression is present, but not necessary for completing a run; skill, knowledge, and, of course, luck, could very much carry you to your first win with little to no meta-progression. If you enjoy survivor-like "bullet heavens" but are looking for something with a bit more structure, I would highly recommend this.

I openly despise roguelikes with a passion, so I started this game with a heavy bias against it. But once I got the hang of it, Spell Disk quickly became one of my favourite games of all time. The roguelike mode is amazing. I love how many unique builds there are to make. I love all the cute little creatures you get to fight. I love the lore and the final bosses. I only wish there was more! More areas, more bosses, more outfits, more weapons. This isn't anything against what the dev's have made, I'm sure getting to this point was very difficult already. It just gets a little samey going through the same 3 areas and the same 9 bosses each run, and I would love to have even more of one of my favourite games to explore. (While I'm glazing everything, my favourite build is Katar, Assassin outfit, Stone Serpent mask. It's so fun dashing and slashing my way through enemies, then finishing them off with a giant stone spike.) If I were to address one issue I have with the roguelike mode, it's that the player can have the Elemental Laser, among other very strong spells, as their starting spell. Some of them are just so strong and versatile that it takes all the fun and nuance out of crafting equipment, cause why make a new build when the elemental laser solos. In all fairness, I can always just not pick up the elemental laser, I just don't think it fits with all the other weaker spells you tend to see as your starter. As for the survivor mode, I personally haven't played it nearly as much as the roguelike mode, and don't enjoy it much. I'm sure other people do, it's just not my cup of tea. I'm also somewhat surprised that the novice equipment is what you start with, because it feels like the strongest item in the room to gain health on level up. Overall, I definitely recommend and absolutely adore Spell Desk. It is more than worth the 13 quid. I even got my dad and gf into it, and they both love it.

I enjoy bullet heaven games as much as the next person, but this one is hard for me to keep being invested in. Set in a random dungeon who knows where in a kingdom of endless war or something, you play as a clone trying to escape with everything trying to kill you for some reason using discs to supply magic support via broken combos. Sure that sounds nice and interesting, but the concept is a bit cluttered and overcomplicated. There are a lot of discs that get activated through different methods and while the spells have auto-homing, there's too much to keep track of while you're also trying to dodge everything going on. There's a lot of items to think about and while the variety is nice, there's not enough resources that can help consistently keep up, especially on higher difficulties. I think the real issue I have is how repetitive the cycle gets after a while. Not only is there the main rouge-lite bullet heaven, there's a the traditional bullet heaven mode of beating random enemies with the same gameplay mechanics. They do have an option to speed up the game speed, but considering the amount of screen clutter you have to deal with, this isn't really worth it. There's also the fact that there isn't much worth unlocking when you get down to it. Long story short, it has too much of one thing without making it worthwhile in the end.
